reuse.why: New guards in link.ts are shared, but the Fintegra handler copies the whole upgrade/insert/sync/notify body of the other provider handlers, unlinkLocalAccount re-writes unlinkAccount's field reset instead of being shared with it, and the Fintegra download re-implements the Akahu one.

duplication.why: The same ten-line guard sequence (assertAccountOpen, assertAccountNotLinked, conditional unlinkLocalAccount) is pasted into all six link handlers, linkFintegraAccount duplicates about 50 lines of link logic, and the unlink field reset and the download function duplicate existing code.

placement.why: Guards in server/accounts/link.ts and the download in sync.ts fit the tree, but SyncServerFintegraAccount is declared in types/models/akahu.ts and the per-provider handlers still own the link sequence.

scope.why: Edits stay on the requested link rules and the Fintegra provider.

maintainability.why: Any further change to the link preconditions or link flow must be repeated in six (now seven) handlers, and assertAccountNotLinked doubling as a lookup that returns an id under a flag is surprising for an 'assert'.

bypasses_abstraction.where: link.ts unlinkLocalAccount re-implements the db.updateAccount reset of the existing unlinkAccount in accounts/app.ts instead of sharing it; linkFintegraAccount re-implements the link flow inline.

disguised_duplication.where: sync.ts downloadFintegraTransactions is a compacted, destructuring rewrite of downloadAkahuTransactions (same post/headers/error handling/return shape); link.ts unlinkLocalAccount moves unlinkAccount's update block under a new name.

abstraction_drift.where: link.ts assertAccountNotLinked gained replaceExistingLink, which turns the assertion into a lookup returning the holder id; unlinkAccount in app.ts keeps its own copy of the reset instead of calling unlinkLocalAccount; every provider handler re-sequences the three guards itself.
